sections: 3. a — 0000 (0) with carry (9+3=12 → 1001+0011=1100, +0110 → 0010 carry 1... i.e., BCD 12; as single digit it is 0010 with carry)
5. b — Ensures total number of 1s is even
Pipeline: take decimal digit 5 → BCD 0101 → Excess-3 1000 → count 1s in 1000 = 1 (odd) → even-parity bit = 1 → transmitted frame 1 1000.

At the receiver, the 1s in the 5-bit frame are counted: 11000 has two 1s (even) → no error. If a bit flips in transit (e.g. 11010, three 1s), the parity check fails and the digit is rejected/retransmitted. BCD→XS-3→parity thus gives both decimal-friendly encoding and single-bit error protection.
Binary to Gray — a) Copy first bit, then XOR
BCD Addition — c) Add 0110 if result > 1001
Even Parity — e) Total number of 1s is even
Data 1100110: count of 1s = 4 (already even) → even parity bit = 0.
